mainTopic: How much dirt a buyer of produce must accept, and רב הונא's rule that a buyer who finds too much may sift out all of it
overview: The עמוד opens at the end of a challenge from the previous עמוד. Someone who removes a pebble from another person's grain must pay the price of wheat for it, which shows that buyers accept some dirt in their produce. The גמרא answers that a buyer accepts a רובע of קטנית per סאה but less than a רובע of עפרורית. A ברייתא allows a full רובע of dirt in עדשים, and the גמרא explains that lentils are different because they are pulled up from the ground. An attempt to prove from this that wheat and barley never get a רובע of dirt is pushed away. Then רב הונא rules that if the buyer sifts out too much waste, he may sift out all of it. Some explain this as the plain law, since the buyer paid for clean produce. Others explain it as a קנס on a seller who must have mixed in the extra. The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a משנה in כלאים that only requires reducing the other seeds, and answers that this is an extra strictness for כלאים. A new challenge to that answer begins at the end of the עמוד and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the pebble challenge: he pays the value of wheat
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a ברייתא from the previous עמוד: someone who removes a pebble from another person's grain must pay him the value of wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: …he must give him the value of wheat!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the גמרא at the last words of a challenge that began on the previous עמוד. The ברייתא says that whoever took a pebble out of someone's grain must pay the owner its volume at the price of wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pebble had stayed in the pile, the owner would have sold it together with the wheat at the price of wheat. So removing it caused him a small loss. This shows that buyers put up with some dirt mixed into their produce, and the גמרא now has to explain how much dirt they accept.

keyTerms.meaning: The value (price) of wheat
He gives him (he must pay him)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the closing punch of a ברייתא quoted on the previous עמוד, and the rest of the case is found there.

phrases.english: He gives him the value of wheat!
phrases.notes: This finishes a case from the previous עמוד about someone who picked a pebble out of another person's grain pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing words of a challenge that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The amount of mixed-in material a buyer must accept, as set out in the previous discussion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying wheat-value for a removed pebble shows that dirt is normally sold together with grain, so buyers must accept some dirt.

steps.title: Legumes up to a quarter, dirt less than a quarter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a buyer accepts a רובע of קטנית per סאה, but only less than a רובע of עפרורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: For legumes, a quarter-קב per סאה. For dirt, less than a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Buyers do accept some dirt, just a smaller amount than the amount of legumes they accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits mixed-in material into two kinds. קטנית is food, so a buyer will tolerate a full רובע of it. Dirt is worthless, so he tolerates only less than a רובע. This way the pebble case still holds, because a little dirt is accepted, but there is a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Legumes (beans and similar), mixed into the grain
A quarter-קב, which is the standard allowance per סאה
Dirt or dust mixed into the produce
Less than a quarter-קב

phrases.notes: That's per סאה of grain. The next ברייתא spells it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pebble challenge by separating the amounts allowed for legumes and for dirt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between types of mixed-in material
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dirt and legumes are accepted in the same amount, a full רובע.
steps.terutzMaskana: A buyer accepts a רובע of legumes, but less than a רובע of dirt.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a full quarter of dirt is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer with a ברייתא saying a buyer of עדשים accepts a רובע of עפרורית per סאה, and suggests the same should apply to wheat and barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that a quarter of dirt is not accepted? But a ברייתא teaches: one who sells produce to another: for wheat, the buyer accepts a quarter-קב of legumes per סאה; for barley, a quarter-קב of chaff per סאה; for lentils, a quarter-קב of dirt per סאה. Doesn't the same rule apply to wheat and barley?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 2 with a ברייתא that allows a full רובע of dirt in lentils. It then argues that the same amount should apply to wheat and barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a buyer accepts less than a רובע of dirt. The ברייתא openly allows a full רובע of dirt for עדשים. The words מאי לאו push the point further: if dirt is allowed at a רובע for lentils, it should be the same for all grains, and then the answer of step 2 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?, which opens a challenge from a source
He (the buyer) accepts upon himself
Chaff, the light husks blown off grain
Lentils
What, is it not the same rule…? This pushes an inference.

phrases.english: One who sells produce to his fellow,
a quarter-kav of legumes per se'a.
a quarter-kav of chaff per se'a.
a quarter-kav of dirt per se'a.
What, is it not the same rule

phrases.notes: Meaning: shouldn't wheat and barley also be allowed a quarter of dirt, the same as lentils?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a buyer accepts less than a רובע of dirt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows a full רובע of dirt in lentils, and that rule should apply to wheat and barley too.

steps.title: Lentils are different because they are pulled from the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עדשים are a special case: they are uprooted, so they naturally come with more dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lentils are different, because they are uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the full רובע of dirt is a special rule just for lentils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lentils are pulled out of the ground roots and all, so dirt comes along with them, and buyers expect that. Wheat and barley are cut above the ground, so less dirt is normal for them. The rule of step 2 therefore stands for ordinary grain.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, used to set apart a special case
They are uprooted (pulled out of the ground)

steps.whatToRemember: A buyer accepts a רובע of קטנית per סאה but less than a רובע of dirt. Lentils are the exception: a full רובע of dirt is accepted for them, because they are uprooted and dirt naturally comes with them.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by limiting the ברייתא's rule about dirt to lentils.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's full רובע of dirt applies to every kind of produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only lentils, which are uprooted, allow a full רובע of dirt. Other grains allow less than a רובע.

steps.title: Trying to prove that wheat and barley do not allow a quarter of dirt
steps.stepSummary: If the only reason עדשים allow a רובע of dirt is that they are uprooted, then wheat and barley, which are not uprooted, should not allow a רובע of עפרורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the reason for lentils is that they are pulled up from the ground, then wheat and barley are different. So we can settle the question: with wheat and barley, the buyer does not accept a quarter of dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the answer from the last step and tries to use it to settle the open question about wheat and barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said עדשים carry a full רובע of dirt because they are uprooted. The גמרא now reasons the other way around: if that is the special reason, then wheat and barley, which lack it, should not get a רובע of עפרורית. This would answer the earlier question and back up the answer of step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Lentils
They are pulled up from the ground (roots and all)
Settle the question from this
Wheat and barley

phrases.english: But then, the reason for lentils
but wheat and barley are not;
so settle the question from this:
with wheat and barley, he does not accept dirt!
phrases.notes: He means a full quarter of dirt per סאה. A smaller amount is already accepted, as step 2 said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a proof out of the answer given in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a buyer of wheat and barley accepts a רובע of עפרורית per סאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about עדשים, together with the reason that עדשים are uprooted

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: lentils were mentioned to set a limit
steps.stepSummary: Wheat and barley may also allow a רובע of dirt. The ברייתא mentioned עדשים only to teach that even they do not get more than a רובע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, wheat and barley also allow dirt. The ברייתא needed to mention lentils because you might have thought that since they are uprooted, the buyer accepts even more than a quarter. It teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The ברייתא's mention of עדשים does not show that wheat and barley allow no dirt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the ברייתא named עדשים because only they allow dirt. The גמרא says the real reason is to set a ceiling: one might think uprooted עדשים allow more than a רובע, so the ברייתא teaches that a רובע is the limit even for them. So the question about wheat and barley stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (used to push back on a proof)
It was necessary for him to say
You might have thought to say
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has now decided that wheat and barley allow dirt. It only shows the proof fails, because the ברייתא could be read either way.

phrases.english: because you might have thought to say:
he should accept even more than a quarter,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 5 by giving another reason the ברייתא mentions עדשים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that wheat and barley do not allow a רובע of עפרורית
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's mention of עדשים can be explained as setting a ceiling of a רובע even for them, not as excluding wheat and barley.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about עדשים proves nothing about wheat and barley. It only teaches that even uprooted עדשים get no more than a רובע of dirt.

steps.title: רב הונא: once the buyer sifts, he sifts out everything
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if the buyer sifts the produce, he may sift out all the waste, not just the extra. Some say this is the plain law and some say it is a penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: If he comes to sift, he sifts all of it. Some say this is the law, and some say it is a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב הונא about a buyer who sifts his produce, and gives two views on why he rules this way. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The allowance of a רובע is not a right the seller keeps once there is too much waste. If the buyer sifts, he may remove all of it. The two views argue whether this follows from what a buyer really expects (דינא) or is a fine on the seller (קנסא).

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives this ruling
To sift (the produce, to remove waste)
The plain law
A penalty

phrases.english: Some say it is the law,
and some say it is a penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אִם בָּא לְנַפּוֹת, מְנַפֶּה אֶת כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what happens once the buyer sifts out the waste.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer who sifts may remove all the waste, not only the amount above a רובע. The reason is debated: דינא or קנסא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the discussion is about which reason is right, so keep both views in mind.

steps.title: Explaining the view that it is the plain law
steps.stepSummary: A buyer pays for clean produce. He lets a רובע go only because it is not worth the trouble. Once there is more and he does sift, he sifts it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is the law: someone who pays money pays for good produce. For a quarter, a person doesn't bother. For more than a quarter, a person does bother. And once he bothers, he bothers with all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first view, that רב הונא's ruling is the plain law (דינא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer never agreed to pay for waste. He lets a רובע go only because sifting is a hassle. Once there is enough waste that he does sift, that reason is gone, so he removes everything and the seller must take it all back.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (coins)
Good, clean produce
Takes the trouble / bothers
A person

phrases.english: Some say it is the law:
and for a quarter, a person doesn't bother,
for more than a quarter, a person does bother;
he bothers with all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ דִּינָא – מַאן דְּיָהֵיב זוּזֵי, אַפֵּירֵי שַׁפִּירֵי יָהֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two views named in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sifting out all the waste is the plain law. The buyer paid for clean produce, and he let a רובע go only because sifting was not worth the trouble.

steps.title: The penalty explanation: the seller mixed in the extra dirt
steps.stepSummary: The second view says the right to sift out all the dirt is a קנס on a seller who mixed in extra dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is a penalty. A quarter of dirt is normal, but more than that is not normal, so the seller must have mixed it in. Since he mixed it in, the רבנן penalized him for all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second view from step 7, that sifting out everything is a קנס (penalty) against the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the buyer always paid for clean produce, so sifting everything is just the plain law. Here a different reason is given. A רובע of dirt happens naturally, but more than that suggests the seller added dirt on purpose. Because he cheated, the רבנן made him lose even the רובע he would normally be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty
Common, normal
He mixed in
The רבנן penalized him

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for רב הונא: either the buyer always paid for clean produce (plain law), or it is a קנס because the seller mixed in the extra dirt.

phrases.english: And some say it is a penalty:
and he is the one who mixed it in;
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller. Extra dirt isn't normal, so we assume he's the one who added it.

phrases.english: and since he mixed it in,
the Rabbis penalized him for all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second reason for רב הונא's ruling, in place of the plain-law reason in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since more than a רובע is unusual, the seller is assumed to have mixed it in, and the רבנן penalized him by letting the buyer sift out all the dirt.

steps.title: A memory aid for the upcoming sources
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a short memory aid that lists key words for the sources it is about to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: All, two documents, of ראבין בר רב נחמן, exploitation and contracting.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. The גמרא is giving a memory aid to set up the list of sources that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old days the גמרא was learned by heart, so a סימן helped people remember the order of the coming sources. Each word hints at a source that will be brought soon. It adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid listing upcoming topics
Documents
Overcharging or exploitation in a sale
Contracting, taking on a job for a set price

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this line as an argument. It is only a list of hint-words for what comes next.

phrases.notes: This is just a memory aid, a few hint-words for the sources coming up. It isn't part of the argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A pause before the גמרא starts bringing sources to test רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; only a memory aid for the sources that follow.

steps.title: Challenge from כלאים: one only needs to reduce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a משנה in כלאים, which says a סאה with a רובע of other seeds only needs to be reduced, not fully cleaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Any סאה of seeds with a quarter of a different kind must be reduced. They assumed that a quarter in כלאים is like more than a quarter here, and it only says 'reduce'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from the laws of כלאים (mixed seeds) to attack רב הונא's ruling that the buyer may sift out everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if seeds have a רובע of another kind, you only need to 'reduce' the other kind, not remove all of it. The גמרא assumed that a רובע in כלאים is like 'too much', the same as more than a רובע in a sale. If there you only remove the extra, then here too the buyer should only sift out the extra, not everything, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a source
The ban on planting different kinds of seeds together
A different kind
He must reduce (lower the amount)
They assumed

phrases.english: Any se'a that has in it
a quarter of a different kind

phrases.notes: This is about seeds for planting. Reduce means taking out some of the other kind, not all of it.

phrases.english: They assumed that a quarter regarding kilayim
is like more than a quarter here,
and it teaches only: he must reduce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's ruling from step 7 using an outside משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that once the buyer sifts, he sifts out all the waste.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a רובע in כלאים equals 'too much' in a sale, and there one only reduces the extra, then in a sale the buyer should only remove the extra too.

steps.title: A quarter in כלאים matches a quarter here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a רובע in כלאים is like a רובע in a sale, a normal amount, so the משנה does not disprove רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, a quarter in כלאים is like a quarter here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the comparison was set up wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed a רובע in כלאים was like 'more than a רובע' in a sale. The גמרא says no: it is like a plain רובע, which is the normal allowed amount. So the משנה is not talking about a case of 'too much', and it says nothing about what to do when there is more, so רב הונא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is similar to, is compared to

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in כלאים does not disprove רב הונא, because its רובע matches the normal allowed רובע in a sale, not the extra amount.
steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, רוֹבַע דְּכִלְאַיִם כִּי רוֹבַע דְּהָכָא דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by rejecting its assumption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumed comparison between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A רובע in כלאים is like more than a רובע in a sale, so one would only remove the extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: A רובע in כלאים is like a plain רובע in a sale, so the משנה is not about 'too much' and does not go against רב הונא.

steps.title: If a quarter is normal, why reduce it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If a רובע per סאה is acceptable, why does the משנה require reducing it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, why must he reduce it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 12. If a רובע of other seeds is a normal, accepted amount, the משנה should not require any change at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said a רובע in כלאים is like a רובע in a sale, so it is not a problem. But the משנה still says 'ימעט', he must reduce it. That word seems to show the רובע is a problem after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you just said is true
Why?
He must reduce (the amount of other seeds)

phrases.english: If so, why must he reduce it?
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if a רובע per סאה really is a normal, acceptable amount, as Step 12 said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a רובע in כלאים is a normal, acceptable amount
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רובע were acceptable, the משנה would not require reducing it. The word ימעט shows something still has to be fixed.

steps.title: Reducing is an extra strictness for כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The requirement to reduce comes only because כלאים is a serious prohibition, not because a רובע is normally a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the severity of כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה requires reducing only as an extra strictness, because כלאים is a serious איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic standard, a רובע is still a normal amount, so the answer in Step 12 stands. The rule to reduce is an added stringency for כלאים in particular. So the משנה is not proof that a רובע is a real problem in a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
Strictness; seriousness
The prohibition of planting different kinds of seeds together

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב הונא's view safe. The extra rule belongs to כלאים alone and does not carry over to buying and selling.

phrases.english: Because of the severity of diverse kinds.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the rule as an extra strictness that applies only to כלאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The requirement to reduce shows that a רובע is a real problem in its own right.
steps.terutzMaskana: A רובע is a normal amount. Reducing it is required only because of how serious כלאים is.

steps.title: Opening a new challenge to the strictness answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge with 'If so', aimed at the answer that reducing is an extra strictness for כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. The גמרא is starting a new challenge against the answer in Step 14, and the rest of that challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אי הכי' mean 'if your answer is true.' Here they point at the idea that the משנה is being extra strict because of כלאים. The גמרא is about to show a problem that follows from that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a קב, the small amount of other seeds being discussed

phrases.notes: This time 'if so' means: if the משנה is being extra strict because כלאים is so serious. The challenge finishes on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the answer of Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the requirement to reduce comes from the seriousness of כלאים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The full argument comes in the next lines. This line only opens it.
